title: A Save Game Is Not a History
description:
Tell the story of campaign checkpoints and history.

Narrative hook and core question: What changes when a campaign must answer not only “can I restore?” but also “what changed, when, and why?”

Research local SQLite campaign/session state, checkpoint snapshots, restore authority, Dolt's role in canonical history, semantic projections or useful diffs, rewind, timeline branching and forking, zero-ops CLI constraints, why a database in the hot gameplay path and a history system are different concerns, and how checkpointing interacts with long campaigns and auditability.

Expected architectural conclusion: a save file restores state. Campaign history also needs explainable change, chronology, and eventually branching.

Boundaries: do not claim unimplemented history UX is shipped. Distinguish current behavior, committed architecture, and future direction. Do not turn this into a generic database article.

Use repository history, PRs, design docs, ADRs, audits, and playtest transcripts as evidence. Verify factual claims against artifacts rather than model memory. Keep the story static, search-indexable, and readable without prior repository knowledge. Follow Joseph's voice rules: analytical and curious, concrete before abstraction, dry humor when earned, deliberate we/I attribution, reflect praise, absorb blame, no em dashes, and no generic LLM prose.
